content: The recommended dosing for African chilies (Ausanil, capsaicin, capsicum) is indication-specific. For post-herpetic pain (shingles), a 3% topical formulation should be applied 4 to 6 times daily. Capsaicin is used topically for conditions such as circulatory problems (peripheral), clotting disorders, diarrhea, digestion problems, fibromyalgia, neuralgias, neuropathies, pain syndromes, and prurigo nodularis. It is also used intranasally for migraines and for the prevention of heart disease. Capsaicin is effective for pain relief. Drug Interactions: Capsicum in combination with ACE inhibitors (e.g., benazepril, captopril, enalapril, fosinopril, imidapril, lisinopril, moexipril, perindopril, quinapril, ramipril, trandolapril) may result in pharmacodynamic synergism. The significance of these interactions is generally unknown, but they may increase the risk of ACE inhibitor-induced cough. Adverse Effects: Common adverse effects include local burning sensation, contact dermatitis, flushing, sweating, urticaria (topical use), and mucous membrane irritation (ocular, nasal, or oral). Gastrointestinal side effects include gastroenteritis, GI irritation, and hepatic damage. Renal damage and bleeding have also been reported. Topical application may cause skin damage, especially on cuts, infected skin, or hypersensitive areas. Contraindications: Capsaicin should not be applied to damaged skin, open wounds, or mucous membranes (mouth, eyes, genitals). It is contraindicated in individuals with hypersensitivity to the product or its excipients, as well as in those with infectious or inflammatory GI conditions (oral use). Precautions: Avoid touching the eyes, nose, mouth, or other mucous membranes after topical application until the product is thoroughly washed off. A burning sensation may occur after application, which varies in intensity among individuals and may be severe. This sensation typically subsides after several days of regular use. Do not tightly wrap or bandage the treated area. Avoid applying heat to the treated area immediately before or after use. Discontinuation and Medical Advice: Discontinue use and consult a healthcare professional if rash, itching, or excessive skin irritation occurs, if the condition worsens, or if symptoms persist for more than 7 days. Seek medical advice if any adverse reactions or concerns arise. Pregnancy and Lactation: Capsaicin is generally considered acceptable for use during pregnancy. Controlled studies in pregnant women have shown no evidence of fetal risk.
